subject: physics

items.q: Why does a gas's pressure rise when heated at constant volume?
items.correct: Particles move faster and hit the walls harder and more often.
items.why: Heat raises particle kinetic energy, so wall collisions are harder/more frequent — higher pressure.

items.q: What happens to temperature while a pure solid melts?
items.correct: It stays constant — energy breaks bonds, not raises temperature.
items.why: Latent heat overcomes forces between particles at constant temperature during a change of state.

items.q: How is a substance's density found?
items.random_wrong: Density is the same as weight.
items.why: Density measures mass packed into a volume; a small dense object can outweigh a large light one.
